title: Simulating hybrid energy systems based on complementary renewable resources
author: During Filho, Beluco

steps.title: Define research problem and performance metric
steps.instruction: Establish the research problem concerning how energetic complementarity influences hybrid system performance, specifying the hybrid system type, the complementarity component to be examined, and the performance parameter (e.g., failure rate, excess energy, cost). Note that Ref [1] seeks the relationship between complementarity and system failure, while Ref [8] examines complementarity effects on excess energy and cost.

steps.title: Specify hybrid system components and demand
steps.instruction: Identify all components of the hybrid system – hydroelectric plant, photovoltaic modules, DC‑AC converters, batteries, and optionally rectifiers, inverters, or fossil‑fuel support – and define the consumer demand profile. Component sizing will be obtained through an optimization that minimizes total net present cost over a 25‑year analysis period.

steps.title: Gather renewable resource parameters
steps.instruction: Collect average, minimum, and maximum values and variability for each renewable resource. For the case study: hydro plant installed capacity 2.22 kW, water flow average 0.380 m³ s⁻¹ (min 0.240, max 0.521); photovoltaic capacity 17.532 kW, solar irradiation average 3.815 kWh m⁻² day⁻¹ (min 1.940, max 5.922). Ref [1] uses a per‑unit system, while Ref [8] provides the absolute values above.

steps.title: Model hourly energy availability
steps.instruction: Choose mathematical or probabilistic models to represent hourly availability over a one‑year horizon with 1‑hour time steps. Idealize water availability with a single sinusoidal function; model solar availability with three sine‑wave functions or with established models such as those of Duffie & Beckman. Recognize that wind or wave resources may require more complex formulations.

steps.title: Select complementarity quantification method
steps.instruction: Adopt an energetic complementarity index, such as the dimensionless index proposed by Beluco et al., focusing on the temporal (time) component of complementarity between the renewable resources.

steps.title: Run simulations and evaluate criteria
steps.instruction: Implement the hybrid system model in a simulation platform (e.g., MATLAB, HOMER Legacy). Simulate the one‑year period with hourly steps, applying the chosen complementarity index. Evaluate performance using appropriate criteria: failure rate in energy supply (Ref [1]), energy shortage and cost of energy (Ref [8]), or reliability as suggested in the literature.

substeps.instruction: Set up the simulation environment (MATLAB, HOMER, etc.).
Input the hourly resource models and system component data.
Run simulations for each complementarity scenario.
Calculate the selected performance criteria for each run.

steps.title: Derive performance limits and analyze results
steps.instruction: Compile the simulation outputs to establish the performance limit of the idealized hybrid system. Plot the performance metric (failure index, energy shortage, cost of energy) versus the time‑complementarity index, acknowledging that the limit is unattainable because the energy profiles are idealized.
